title: NAM low end: re-amp comparison
subtitle: A 3-minute bass DI re-amped through the pedal with four conversions of the Ampeg SVT-VR Classic (Normal) NAM model and the Ampeg SVT Beta52 cab IR, against the original model and IR run in software on exactly what the pedal heard. Every take is time-aligned and loudness-matched before comparing.
method: Rig: a bass DI recording played from an audio interface into the pedal's input and recorded from the pedal's USB audio (48 kHz). One session, the same cables and levels for every take, nothing clipping.

Takes: the same model converted three ways and uploaded to user AMP slots: open-stomp 0.5 (octave-weighted fit), open-stomp 0.4 (the same optimiser with the old flat weighting) and the official Stomp Manager app. The cab is the same IR converted by open-stomp 0.4, except '0.5: NAM + IR', which uses the IR as 0.5 converts it (fit limited to 30 Hz – 16 kHz). Repeated takes of the same upload agree within 0.01 dB, so the rig didn't drift.

Reference: the original .nam file run in software on the pedal's own dry input (recorded with the AMP and CAB blocks off) at the model's input level, the pedal's DC blocker, then the full original IR file (44.1 kHz, resampled). So it hears exactly what the pedal heard.

Each take is aligned to the dry take by band-envelope correlation and loudness-matched to the reference over the playing parts. The comparisons are magnitude only (spectra and band levels): the conversions don't reproduce the model's phase, so a null test would mostly measure phase.
Moment-to-moment error: 100 ms windows every 50 ms, third-octave bands from 40 Hz, only bands within 40 dB of that moment's loudest reference band.

Where the rest of the gap is: run in software on this same input, the 0.5 NAM upload alone is within ±0.5 dB of the model from 50 to 126 Hz. The remaining dip at 56–80 Hz comes from the cab: the pedal plays only 384 taps (8 ms) of an IR, too short for the Beta52's resonance above its steep low cut. Even a perfect NAM through that IR is 7 dB short at 63 Hz.
